name: Stone
flavor: Grey. Heavy. Karl's best friend and most frequent conversation partner.

name: Stick
flavor: A stick of exceptional quality. So says Karl, and he has seen many sticks.

name: Dry grass
flavor: Bone-dry and highly flammable. For now, Karl uses it as a pillow.

name: Water
flavor: Wet. Karl has tasted it and can confirm: very wet.

name: Clay
flavor: Soft and mouldable. Much like Karl's relationship with good ideas.

name: Berries
flavor: Possibly edible. Karl uses the bird test: if the bird survives, it's lunch.

name: Grubs
flavor: They wriggle. Karl watches them a little too long and a little too fondly.

name: Wild boar
flavor: A boar that has observed Karl for three days and remains unimpressed.

name: Sparks
flavor: Tiny stars that live for half a second. Karl applauds every time.
note: Stone Age fire-starting struck flint against pyrite — two ordinary stones really can make sparks.

name: Fire
flavor: Warm, glowing, and not at all fond of being touched. Karl discovered that part personally.
note: Humans have controlled fire for at least 400,000 years — traces from Wonderwerk Cave suggest up to a million.

name: Stone axe
flavor: A rock on a stick. Humanity's first subscription to tools.
note: The oldest stone tools are over 2.5 million years old — older than modern humans themselves.

name: Spear
flavor: Pointy at one end. Karl held the wrong one first.
note: The Schöningen spears from Germany are about 300,000 years old — the world's oldest preserved hunting weapons.

name: Meat
flavor: Fresh from a boar that underestimated Karl. A mistake nobody saw coming.
note: Eating meat accelerated human brain evolution — more energy per bite than any plant.

name: Roast meat
flavor: Crispy outside, juicy inside. Karl has invented gastronomy and is never going back.
note: Cooked food gave humans more calories for less chewing — a possible key to our big brains.

name: Roasted grubs
flavor: Crispy. Nutty. Karl says 'mmm'. The narrator says nothing, very loudly.
note: Around two billion people eat insects today — grubs are rich in protein and climate-friendly.

name: Mud
flavor: Clay plus water. Karl calls it 'soft dirt' and is very proud of the name.
note: Mud and clay were humanity's first building materials — sun-dried bricks are over 9,000 years old.

name: Mud bath
flavor: Karl rolls thoroughly. He calls it skincare. The boar nods in approval.
note: Pigs really do use mud baths as sunscreen and insect protection — early humans possibly did too.

name: Pottery
flavor: Baked clay that holds water. Karl's first pot is crooked, and he loves it.
note: The world's oldest pottery is about 20,000 years old, found in Xianrendong Cave in China.

name: Steam
flavor: The water hisses and vanishes into the air. Karl is deeply offended on the water's behalf.
note: Steam power was demonstrated in antiquity with Heron's aeolipile — but only changed the world in the 1700s.

name: Ore
flavor: Glittering stones from the rock face. Karl thinks it's decoration. It's the future.
note: The oldest known mines are over 40,000 years old — long before anyone knew what metal was.

name: Copper
flavor: Shiny, reddish, and bendable. Karl has tried biting it. Twice.
note: Humans have worked copper for almost 10,000 years — the oldest finds come from Anatolia.

name: Bronze
flavor: Harder than copper, fancier than stone. Karl made a lump and shows it to everyone.
note: Bronze — copper alloyed with tin — emerged around 3300 BC and gave its name to an entire era.

name: Grub farm
flavor: A clay bowl of well-groomed grubs. Karl has named them all. Every one is called Bent.
note: Insect farming is a growing industry today — grubs turn food waste into protein better than any livestock.

name: Log
flavor: A fallen tree trunk. Karl has claimed it by sitting on it.

name: Neighbour
flavor: Another caveman. His name is Ugh. He communicates mostly through disappointed grunts.

name: Round stone
flavor: Polished perfectly round by the river. Karl calls it 'the good rock' and guards it jealously.
note: River pebbles really are rounded by erosion — tumbling water does in centuries what a stonemason does in days.

name: Wheel
flavor: It rolls. It ROLLS. Karl has chased it across the valley twice already.
note: The wheel arrived surprisingly late — around 3500 BC in Mesopotamia, long after farming and pottery.

name: Planks
flavor: Flat wood. Karl split a log and is now the valley's leading carpenter, by default.
note: The oldest known woodworking, including split planks, predates modern humans — Neanderthals built with wood 400,000 years ago.

name: Crafting table
flavor: Four planks arranged in a square. Karl feels a strange urge to punch a tree.
note: A certain block game with crafting tables became the best-selling video game of all time — over 300 million copies.

name: Cart
flavor: Wheels plus planks. It carries things so Karl doesn't have to. Civilization's true purpose, achieved.
note: The earliest wagons appear around 3400 BC — and spread across Europe and Mesopotamia within a few centuries.

name: Footmobile
flavor: A foot-powered stone-age car. Ugh rides shotgun. Karl makes engine noises with his mouth. Yabba dabba... something.
note: The Flintstones (1960) was the first animated series in TV primetime — and its foot-powered car became an icon.

name: Standing stone
flavor: A tall stone, raised on end for no practical reason. Karl touches it carefully, then throws a bone in the air. He doesn't know why.
note: Thousands of menhirs — raised standing stones — dot Europe, some over 6,000 years old. Their purpose is still debated.

name: Stone circle
flavor: A circle of standing stones. Karl aligned them with the sunrise by accident and takes full credit.
note: Stonehenge was built in stages from about 3000 BC — with stones hauled up to 200 kilometres.

name: Pet boar
flavor: The boar, bribed with berries into friendship. Karl has named him Dino. He answers to nothing.
note: Pigs were domesticated around 8,500 BC — among the first animals after dogs.

name: Fish
flavor: Speared straight from the river. Karl eats it raw and declares it 'sushi', ten thousand years too early.
note: Humans have fished for over 40,000 years — bone analysis of early modern humans shows regular freshwater fish dinners.

name: Hide cloak
flavor: A warm boar hide. Karl wears it like a cape and practices dramatic turns.
note: Genetics dates clothing to at least 100,000 years ago — scientists worked it out by studying when clothing lice evolved.

name: Cave painting
flavor: Berry juice on stone. It's either a boar, a sunset, or Ugh. Karl refuses to explain his art.
note: The oldest known cave paintings are over 45,000 years old — found in Sulawesi, Indonesia.

name: Drum
flavor: A hollow log plus a stick. Karl has rhythm. The valley disagrees.
note: Drums are among humanity's oldest instruments — alligator-skin drums from China date to 5500 BC.

name: Rock band
flavor: Karl on drums, Ugh on backing grunts. They play rocks. They are, literally, a rock band.
note: The Rolling Stones formed in 1962 — and are still rolling. Some stones gather no moss.

name: Cave brew
flavor: Berries, left in a pot slightly too long. Karl calls it juice. The juice disagrees.
note: The world's oldest known beer residue is 13,000 years old, found in Raqefet Cave in Israel — possibly older than bread.

name: Stone age party
flavor: Two guests, one brew, infinite confidence. The boar is the bouncer.
note: Archaeologists have found evidence of large prehistoric feasts — including a 12,000-year-old burial banquet with 71 tortoises.

name: Pot friend
flavor: A pot with a face painted on it. Karl tells it everything. Its name is Wilson.
note: In Cast Away (2000), Tom Hanks' best co-star was a volleyball named Wilson — proof that loneliness is a great animator.

name: Boomerang
flavor: A bent stick that comes back. Karl has invented losing things professionally.
note: The oldest known boomerang is 23,000 years old, carved from mammoth tusk — found in a cave in Poland.

name: Grub stand
flavor: The valley's first restaurant. One item on the menu. Two stars, scratched on the rock outside.
note: Ready-to-eat street food is ancient — Pompeii alone had around 80 thermopolia, the Roman world's snack bars.

name: Wild grain
flavor: Tiny seeds on stalks. A woman from the next valley claims you can eat them. Karl is skeptical.

name: Ox
flavor: Big, strong, and surprisingly willing to cooperate. More than can be said for Karl.
